courses.pronunciationHelp: Pinyin keeps underlying third tones: nǐ hǎo starts with a rising tone in speech. 一/不 show common spoken changes; unmarked syllables are neutral. Listen to whole phrases. Ask a Mandarin speaker for feedback—the app doesn’t grade your voice.

courses.label: English → Spoken Palestinian Arabic
courses.testText: مرحبا، كيفك؟ بدّي كاسة ميّ لو سمحت.
courses.pronunciationHelp: Palestinian everyday speech, with an urban-leaning reading. ā/ī/ū/ē/ō are long vowels; sh, kh and gh are single sounds. ḥ is a deep, breathy h; ʿ is ع; ʾ is a glottal stop. ṣ/ḍ/ṭ/ẓ are emphatic consonants; doubled letters are held longer. The reading usually uses ʾ for ق; q, g and k occur in other local accents. Short vowels and j also vary locally. Arabic spelling is partly unvoweled: follow the Latin reading for the intended form. Speaker/addressee gender is labeled on cards. Device and Google voices may use formal Arabic; they are not verified Palestinian models. Ask a local speaker to check your pronunciation.
courses.audioNote: Arabic audio may use formal pronunciation. The Latin reading shows the intended Palestinian form.
